events.ai_basis: The core 585-fiber argument is mine, while the remaining arguments are from GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

why: The statement has two parts: whether a perfect cuboid exists, and the associated cuboid conjectures (three of them, per the linked article). Every in-window claim of full nonexistence is set aside. Yelle conceded in v2. Muhammad, Liu and Reed each show several F10 signals: self-posted with no uptake, approaches that keep changing or exotic methods, and in Reed's case a Lean file whose main theorem assumes its key steps. Reed's Gemini acknowledgement covers only formalization and editing, so its role is none. The fiber theorems of Peschmann and Cipollini each exclude perfect cuboids on infinitely many tuples within explicitly named fibers. That is a restriction of Part 1, so I scored them case, not instances, and both authors say they are not the global result. In Cipollini, the author credits the models with the arguments for the fibers outside their own 585, which is mathematics that is in the result, so it is assisted. Asiryan's two irreducibility papers each claim one of the three named conjectures, so they are case. Excluding one factorization pattern settles no restriction of the conjecture (none), and the height-bounded search is instances. Riley Tao (10 January 2024) and de Grey et al. (6 January 2024) both predate the snapshot.
doubts: Scoring fiber-bounded exclusions as case rather than instances was a close call. Each fiber is an infinite family settled by proof (rank-zero arguments), not by search, which decided it. The Cipollini quote came through a summarising fetch and has not been checked verbatim. Asiryan's v3 theorem is stated more broadly than Cuboid conjecture 1, but it contains the conjecture's setting.
